article_briefs.brief: Tata Motors raised its all‑cash voluntary tender offer for Iveco to €14.40 per share, valuing the transaction at €3.91 billion. The revised price represents a 33.47 % premium to Iveco’s share price on 17 July 2025 and a 6.77 % premium to the price on 29 July 2025. Funding will be provided via an €85 million credit facility with MUFG Bank Ltd, and the company said the offer will not be increased further.

Tata Motors’ €3.91‑billion bid for Iveco is described as its “best and final” offer of €14.40 a share. The deal’s success now hinges on shareholder votes that could lower the acceptance threshold from 95 % to 80 % if a restructuring proposal is approved. Exor holds 27.06 % of Iveco’s shares and supports the deal, while large minority shareholders holding about 20 % could determine whether the required support is achieved.

Stellantis India, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd (TMPV) and its subsidiary Tata Passenger Electric Mobility Ltd signed a definitive agreement expanding their partnership into advanced vehicle technology and product collaboration. TMPV will provide Stellantis access to its product technology and vehicle architecture, with vehicles to be manufactured in India at the 50:50 joint‑venture Fiat India Automobiles Private Limited (FIAPL) in Pune for more than 50 global markets.

Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles and Stellantis have expanded their long‑standing partnership with a definitive agreement that combines Tata’s vehicle architecture and technology capabilities with Stellantis’ global product development expertise. The collaboration will develop vehicles in India for over 50 markets, with manufacturing at the FIAPL joint venture, and leverages Stellantis’ 14‑brand portfolio and worldwide engineering network.

Tata Motors raised its offer for Iveco to €14.40 per share on 9 October, a 2 % increase after activist Petrus Advisers rejected the original price. The revised price is the “best and final” offer. Three major shareholders—Davidson Kempner, Syquant Capital and Petrus Advisers—hold about 20.4 % of Iveco’s shares and have not tendered, leaving total acceptances at 28.4 % with the deadline on 26 October.

key_points.text: Tata Motors increased its all‑cash takeover offer for Iveco to €14.40 per share, valuing the transaction at €3.91 billion, representing a 33.47 % premium to Iveco’s share price on 17 July 2025 and a 6.77 % premium to the price on 29 July 2025.
The increase is funded through an €85 million credit facility with MUFG Bank Ltd, GIFT Branch, and Tata Motors said the revised price will not be increased further.

Tata Motors describes the €14.40 per share bid as its “best and final” offer, with no higher bid expected, and the deal now hinges on shareholder acceptance, with a possible reduction of the acceptance threshold from 95 % to 80 % if shareholders approve a restructuring proposal.

Exor, Iveco’s largest shareholder, holds 27.06 % of shares (43 % voting rights) and has tendered its stake; three other large shareholders (Davidson Kempner, Syquant Capital, Petrus Advisers) together own about 20.4 % and have not tendered, leaving total acceptances at 28.4 % of shares.
If the acquisition completes, it would create a global commercial‑vehicle group with roughly €21 billion of annual revenue and about 5,90,000 vehicles sold per year.

Tata Motors and Stellantis signed a definitive agreement to collaborate on advanced vehicle technology and product development, giving Stellantis access to Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles’ architecture and technology, with manufacturing slated at the 50:50 FIAPL joint venture in Pune for export to more than 50 global markets.

The partnership builds on a February 2026 MoU and aims to combine Tata’s Indian engineering and manufacturing capabilities with Stellantis’s global product development expertise across its 14‑brand portfolio.

article_briefs.brief: Tata Motors needs to win over silent shareholders that represent roughly three‑quarters of the non‑voting pool to reach the 80% acceptance required to fully acquire and delist Iveco. About 52.9% of Iveco’s common shares have backed the deal, while silent shareholders own roughly 27% of shares that have not voted. If only 66.67% is reached, Tata can waive the higher threshold but would not be able to squeeze out minority shareholders or delist Iveco.

Brokerages preview Tata Motors CV Q2 FY27 results, expecting profit after tax to rise up to 44% YoY and revenue to grow 44‑45% YoY, driven by ~43% volume expansion. Margins are projected to stay under pressure despite a 2.5% price hike, with differing views on EBITDA margin trends.

Two hedge funds and an activist investor hold about 20.4% of Iveco’s common shares and could earn roughly €63 million at the €14.40 per‑share offer, plus €288 million in extraordinary dividends. Their decision to tender shares is critical for Tata Motors to reach the 80% threshold; as of 21 Oct, shareholders had tendered about 33.4% of Iveco’s shares, with the offer closing on 26 Oct.

A market roundup lists Tata Motors among several stocks that investors will watch on 23 Oct as companies report September‑quarter earnings, credit rating updates, fundraising plans, regulatory developments and new business wins.
Tata Motors reported Q2 FY27 consolidated profit of ₹1,257 crore, with revenue up 36.3%. Shares fell about 4% ahead of the results, trading around ₹397.80.
